column2: Manish s/o Rajkumar Bhagwani and Ors. v. State of Maharashtra (through PSO, PS Washim, District Washim) and Anr.
column12: Whether the FIR and charge-sheet under ss 498A, 323, 504 and 506 IPC can be quashed when the spouses divorced and settled while the application was pending.
column13: FIR and charge-sheet quashed: after the divorce, a ?6 lakh full-and-final settlement and a joint affidavit, the offence is not serious or anti-social, so continuing the prosecution serves no purpose.

column2: Shrikant Gajanan Pendor and 3 Others v. State of Maharashtra (through PSO, Padoli, District Chandrapur) and Sau. Tina Shrikant Pendor
column12: Whether the cruelty FIR and trial under ss 498A and 504 IPC should be quashed against the husband and his relatives, given that the mother-in-law died during the case.
column13: Quashed only for the two sisters-in-law because the allegations against them were vague and omnibus; refused for the husband because specific incidents were alleged against him. The mother-in-law’s part was disposed of on her death.
column14: Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam v. State of Bihar (2022) 6 SCC 599

column2: Gaurav s/o Arun Bute and Ors. v. State of Maharashtra (through PSO, PS Chimur) and Anr.
column12: Whether the FIR for cruelty, cheating and dowry harassment should be quashed against the husband and six of his relatives when the allegations against the relatives are general.
column13: Quashed for the six relatives because the allegations were general, vague and sweeping, with no specific acts or amounts; refused for the husband, against whom a specific allegation (concealing his impotence) was made.
column14: Dara Lakshmi Narayana v. State of Telangana (2024 SCC OnLine SC 3682)

column2: Akash Bhimrao Ingle and Ors. v. State of Maharashtra (through PSO, PS Akot File, Akola) and Anr.
column12: Whether the cruelty FIR under s 85 BNS (the old s 498A IPC) can stand against the husband and nine relatives when the allegations are general and the husband is only said to have barely spoken to his wife.
column13: FIR quashed against all ten applicants: general, omnibus allegations that name relatives without giving them a role are not enough, and not talking to the wife is not ill-treatment.
column14: None cited in the judgment

column2: Sunita Kumari and Others v. State of Maharashtra and Others
column12: Whether distant relatives of the husband, who live apart from the wife, can get a cruelty FIR and pending charge-sheet quashed.
column13: Application dismissed with ?10,000 costs: distant relatives still count as “relatives” under s 498A, mental cruelty need not happen in person, and the FIR showed a prima facie case against each applicant.
column14: U. Suvetha v. State by Inspector of Police (2009) 6 SCC 757

column2: Shaikh Shaukat s/o Majit @ Majid Patel and Ors. v. State of Maharashtra and Anr.
column12: Whether proceedings under section 498A, 323, 504 and 506 IPC can be quashed on a settlement reached after the trial court had already convicted the husband and his parents, while their appeal was still pending.
column13: Trial proceedings and the FIR was quashed and held section 482 CrPC can be used after conviction if an appeal is pending, and the settlement (Khula, ?3.25 lakh plus meher, wife’s no-objection) was voluntary and genuine.
column14: Ramawatar v. State of Madhya Pradesh, 2021 SCC OnLine SC 966

column2: Vrushali Jayesh Kore v. State of Maharashtra
column12: Whether an FIR under section 498A, 323, 504, 406 and 506 IPC and the Dowry Prohibition Act can be quashed against the husband’s married sister, who was dragged into the matrimonial dispute.
column13: FIR quashed against the applicant and held even taken at face value the allegations disclose no evidence of any crime committed by her, and letting the case run would misuse the criminal process into a personal graduges.
column14: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335

column13: Quashing of FIR and criminal proceeding and held that the wife presented her affidavit in court without any objections to it, and as the matter is between individuals, the continuation of the case is an abuse of procedure.

column2: Rushik Rajendra Shah and Ors. v. Ruchika Rushik Shah and Anr.
column12: Whether an FIR and charge-sheet under secction 498A, 325, 323, 307 and 504 IPC and the Dowry Prohibition Act can be quashed after charges were framed, when the spouses had divorced by mutual consent and settled.
column13: FIR, charge sheet and other proceedings set aside and held that the crimes are not heinous, are of a personal nature, the terms of consent are real and cover the interests of the child, and there is no objection from the wife.

column2: Vaibhav Gopaldas Mundada and Ors. v. State of Maharashtra and Anr.

column13: Appeal to FIR dismissed in respect of all five appellants because the charges were general and omnibus in nature with no dates or acts of cruelty mentioned and the chat and documents revealed that it was an oppression case
column14: Pradeep Kumar Kesarwani v. State of Uttar Pradesh, 2025 SCC OnLine SC 1947

column13: FIR and criminal case quashed since matrimonial dispute was amicably resolved by parties through mutual compromise

column2: Jalendra Sakharam Khare & Ors. v. State of Maharashtra & Shital Khare
column11: s 482 CrPC; s 12, 23 Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005; s 498A IPC

column14: Madan Mohan Abbot v. State of Punjab, (2008) 4 SCC 582

column2: Ganesh s/o Chandrakant Sadawarti & 4 Ors. v. State of Maharashtra & Anr.
column12: Whether the FIR under ss 498A, 323, 504 and 506 read with s 34 IPC can be quashed against the husband and his relatives when the allegations are general and the wife had taken a recorded ?8 lakh settlement.

column14: Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam v. State of Bihar (2022) 6 SCC 599

column2: Prasanna S/o Vijay Joshi and 2 Others v. State of Maharashtra (through PSO, PS Civil Lines, Akola) and Anr.

column2: Vandana Rameshchandra Oza and Ors. v. State of Maharashtra and Anr.
column12: Whether FIR No. 138/2023 (ss 498A, 323, 504, 506 r/w s 34 IPC) and the pending chargesheet can be quashed against the husband’s alleged paramour and the husband’s married sister and her husband.
column13: FIR, chargesheet and RCC No. 476/2025 quashed against all three applicants: a paramour is not a “relative” (status by blood, marriage or adoption), there was no dowry demand or cruelty by the sister and brother-in-law, and the omnibus allegations had no dates or places; ss 323/504/506 are non-cognizable.

column2: Vaishali Janbaji Gawande v. State of Maharashtra and Anr.
column3: 2024 SCC OnLine Bom 2766; 2024 LiveLaw (Bom) 440 (Criminal Application (APL), Chandrapur proceedings; number not in sources seen)
column12: Whether the chargesheet under s 498A IPC (now ss 85 and 86 BNS) can stand against the husband’s paramour, a married woman who is not his relative.
column13: Chargesheet quashed against the paramour alone: s 498A applies only to the husband or his relative, and a paramour in an extra-marital affair is not a relative of the husband.
column14: U. Suvetha v. State by Inspector of Police & Anr. (2009) 6 SCC 757

column2: Payal w/o Umakant M. v. State of Maharashtra and Anr.
column12: Whether an FIR under s 498A IPC can stand against the husband’s sister and her husband, who live separately, when the only allegation against them is general instigation.
column13: FIR quashed against the sister-in-law and her husband: relatives living at a different place and accused only of sweeping, general instigation cannot be prosecuted under s 498A.
